transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m having a hard time keeping my mind on one thing. Like, at work I’ll be fixing a rendering bug, and then a Slack ping or some color on the screen, or even a siren outside, just pulls me off into some other idea before I finish the line of code. It’s been… hard to get anything done.
When your attention shifts like that, does it feel like your mind is racing or you're unusually excited or energized, or does it feel more like you're feeling anxious or down?

More energized, I guess. Most days I feel kind of… lit up, like I’m onto something and everything’s finally lining up. But I get irritated fast when people slow me down—my wife, coworkers—with all the “process” stuff. It feels like they’re getting in the way.
Have you noticed any periods lately where you felt you needed less sleep than usual, or where you felt rested even after only a few hours of sleep?
I don’t know. I haven’t really been tracking it. Maybe some nights are shorter, but I’m not sure I’d say I feel rested exactly.

Have you had any distinct periods recently—lasting at least a few days—where your mood was unusually high, irritable, or energized, and you were doing more things than usual, like taking on new projects, talking more, or feeling like you didn’t need much sleep?

Yeah… I guess so. Most days I feel kind of lit up, like I’m unstoppable, like Glendale finally caught up with what I’ve been building. But I get irritated fast when my wife or coworkers slow me down with all the “process” stuff. I snap harder than I probably should.

latest_inference.note: The patient endorsed distinct periods of elevated mood, increased energy, irritability, and possible decreased need for sleep, which aligns with a hypomanic episode. This makes F31.81 (Bipolar II disorder, current episode hypomanic) the most fitting diagnosis. Other candidates (F34.81, F41.9, F06.81) are less consistent with the reported symptoms.
